## Svelte 5 rewrite

Please note that [the Svelte codebase is currently being rewritten for Svelte 5](https://svelte.dev/blog/runes). Changes should target Svelte 5, which lives on the default branch (`main`).

If your PR concerns Svelte 4 (including updates to [svelte.dev.docs](https://svelte.dev/docs)), please ensure the base branch is `svelte-4` and not `main`.

### Before submitting the PR, please make sure you do the following

- [ ] It's really useful if your PR references an issue where it is discussed ahead of time. In many cases, features are absent for a reason. For large changes, please create an RFC: https://github.com/sveltejs/rfcs
- [ ] Prefix your PR title with `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, or `docs:`.
- [ ] This message body should clearly illustrate what problems it solves.
- [ ] Ideally, include a test that fails without this PR but passes with it.

### Tests and linting

- [ ] Run the tests with `pnpm test` and lint the project with `pnpm lint`

comments: Typescript isn't allowed in the svelte template, so this is expected. 🙃

> Typescript isn't allowed in the svelte template, so this is expected. 🙃

It is in Svelte 5. I've been using it everywhere else in the template. It's one of its best new features.

@dummdidumm @gtm-nayan Guys, can you please check this again? I installed versions 38 and 40 of Svelte and still get a syntax error for doing this. The syntax error is `';' expected.ts(1005)` System: OS: Windows 11 10.0.22621 CPU: (16) x64 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12650H Memory: 6.59 GB / 15.63 GB Binaries: Node: 18.14.2 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE npm: 9.7.1 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.CMD Browsers: Edge: Chromium (120.0.2210.144) Internet Explorer: 11.0.22621.1 npmPackages: svelte: ^5.0.0-next.40 => 5.0.0-next.40 My typescript version is also `^5.3.3` and the code is simple ```svelte
```

`bind:this={searchInput}`

When I do

`let searchInput = $state<HTMLInputElement>();`

Then it warns me `searchInput` is possibly undefined when I try to use it

When I do

`let searchInput: HTMLInputElement = $state();`

Then in the declaration it tells me `Type 'HTMLInputElement | undefined' is not assignable to type 'HTMLInputElement'`

I understand **why** these occur, but there has to be a correct way of doing this in svelte 5. Had no problems in svelte 4. I either deal with the red squiggle and error in every typescript check in every file, or I check if it's truthy in every call, which I shouldn't have to do since it's already bound to the element and the functions I'm calling are after page load.
@justingolden21 Either do `let searchInput = $state() as HTMLInputElement` or assert it as non null I think like this `let searchInput: HTMLInputElement = $state()!;`.

> let searchInput = $state() as HTMLInputElement

@Antonio-Bennett Thank you so much! This works perfectly. Can't believe I didn't think of this and couldn't find it from anything online or chatgpt 😅 You're a lifesaver! 🙏

review_comments: I tried removing all AST nodes right after parsing in a post-process step, but it failed because of this - if you have an idea how to solve this, I'm all ears
That's for removing it during parsing right? We could do one pass after the whole file is parsed.
Mhm maybe. I removed it after an expression/the script tag was parsed, but doing it after the whole thing is parsed could maybe work.. would you mind trying it out?
